title: Stream priming queue starvation causing multi-tenant first-token lag
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Summary:
Several customers (hosted and dedicated tiers, plus one Private VPC) reported large increases in first-token time (TTFT) and reduced tokens/sec over the last 48 hours. The spike correlates with a priming change that increased background prefetches of model KV and token priming streams for recent warm-start optimization. Visible across small and medium models with multiplexing enabled.

Impact:
- Intermittent first-byte delays from 200ms -> 800ms+ for affected sessions.
- Sustained tokens/sec drop for multiplexed workers under 60% utilization during spikes.
- Customer escalations opened: CUST-1223 (SaaS analytics), CUST-1237 (B2B chat), CUST-1241 (enterprise on Private).

Scope:
- Hosted API region eu-west-1 and us-east-1; Dedicated customer pools with multiplexing; one Private VPC deployment using runtime-1.21 had the same symptom after config sync.

Investigation notes (what we've looked at):
- Telemetry: router queue length histogram shows bursts of long-lived priming streams occupying multiplex queue slots for 10-30s, blocking low-latency interactive streams.
- Kernel metrics: heavy kernel-context switches when priming prefetches hit quantized-kernel fallback path, causing eviction thrash.
- Recent change: rollout of priming-prefetch parallelism increase in runtime-1.21 -> 1.22 (internal PR #5218).
- Repro: local stress test with synthetic traffic reproduces TTFT spike by ramping concurrent priming requests to >30 per worker.

Root cause hypothesis:
Concurrent priming prefetches (intended to reduce cold-starts) can monopolize multiplex queue slots and trigger kernel fallback/eviction cycles on quantized models, causing starvation for short interactive requests. The router currently treats priming streams as equal priority which exacerbates heap/affinity inversion under contention.

Mitigation plan (hotfix):
1) Immediate: Patch router to treat priming-prefetch streams as best-effort with a configurable concurrency cap per worker and model-variant (hotfix PR #5283). This reduces simultaneous priming to 4 per worker.
2) Short-term: Add backpressure token for priming to prevent queue starvation and expose metric priming_in_flight.
3) Medium-term: Implement first-token fast-path that prioritizes short interactive streams in the multiplexer and bypasses heavy prefetch when latency SLO is close to breach (design doc in Confluence: /r/confluence/RW-PrimingFastPath).
4) Rollback: If the hotfix increases cold starts, rollback PR #5218 and re-evaluate prefetch heuristics.

Testing and rollout strategy:
- Canary patch to 5% of hosted traffic (eu-west-1) and one Dedicated customer pool (non-production) for 2 hours, monitor TTFT p50/p95, tokens/sec, and priming_in_flight.
- If stable, increment to 50% over 3 hours, then full rollout.
- Private customer (CUST-1241) will be provided a tarball and patch instructions; schedule a maintenance window if accepted.

Observability and dashboards:
- Dashboards to watch: /dashboards/runtime/ttft-by-variant, /dashboards/router/queue-occupancy, /dashboards/kernel/eviction-events.
- Alerts: create alert RTT-PRIMING-TTFt if p95 TTFT > 700ms for 5m and priming_in_flight > 8.

Customer comms:
- Drafted incident notes for CUST-1223 and CUST-1237. Support to inform CUST-1241 that a patch is available and recommend a maintenance slot.

Next steps:
- Merge hotfix PR #5283 after 1 engineering review. (owner: Mateo Chen)
- Deploy canary and monitor for 4 hours, collect traces for affected sessions. (owner: SRE oncall)
- Ship short-term backpressure metric change PR #5290 (owner: Priya Rao).

Artifacts and links:
- Hotfix PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/5283
- Revert candidate (prior prefetch change): https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/5218
- Stress test scenario: https://ci.redwood-inference/internal/job/priming-stress/742
- Confluence: /r/confluence/RW-PrimingFastPath
